courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: Foundation English for University Studies
courses.description: This course aims to lay the comprehensive English language foundation needed for university studies by engaging students in multi-modal learning activities. Learning topics include the writing process, expository writing, critical listening, reading and response, and features of spoken English. Coursework consists of critical reading, expository essay writing, and individual presentation tasks. This course is compulsory for first-year students, except those who have attained HKDSE English level 5 or above or its equivalence. This course is a prerequisite for Level Two and Three courses.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Not for students who have taken ELTU1002
courses.course_syllabus:
Learning topics include:

Module 1 - The Writing Process
Module 2 - Critical Listening, Reading and Response
Module 3 - Features of Spoken English
courses.feedback_evaluation:
1. Post-course questionnaire (PCQ)
2. Course and teaching evaluation (CTE) questionnaire

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: English Through Film, Television, and Society
courses.description: As an alternative for Year 2 students of the Faculty of Social Science and Faculty of Arts, this course is designed to introduce students to the role of film and television in the contemporary society. Broadly speaking, it is a course that examines the relationship between cinema and television as two art forms and the society. In this connection, various genres of film and television will be covered. The course will specifically explore a) the text structures and language of the two art forms; b) the way in which those texts are produced; and c) the way in which they are consumed by critical viewers.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: ELTU1001 or ELTU1002 or exemption from these courses
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. analyze cinematic art and conduct an in-depth analysis of a chosen film.
2. appreciate and analyze a school of thought of cinema.
3. discuss various social themes of different important films from past to present.
4. evaluate cinematic language and the key elements of a narrative film.
5. write an essay highlighting their analysis of their chosen film.
6. present their analysis of the chosen film.
courses.course_syllabus:
Learning topics include:

1. Women and feminism in the romance genre.
2. Anthologies and their themes.
3. Political satire and political thriller as a genre.
4. Academy Award nominated and winning films: what and why?
5. The role and importance of musicals.

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: Language Awareness for Teachers 1: Listening and Speaking
courses.description: This course provides prospective teachers of English with the opportunity to enhance their listening and speaking skills in English. Specifically, it will focus on effective strategies for listening and responding in an appropriate and professional manner in academic settings. Coursework will include completing listening assignments, conducting panel discussions, and giving individual and group presentations on a wide range of topics, including those related to teaching English in Hong Kong.
courses.course_syllabus:
List of Topics

Introducing concepts of listening

Identifying your own listening habits

- Explore key concepts of listening which will enhance students’ language awareness of this learning modality. Three aspects will be introduced: linguistic knowledge, genre knowledge and discourse knowledge.

- Identify students’ own listening habits with the aim of improving listening with focused learning

Exploring listening strategies (1)

- Explore listening problems that impede comprehension and seek ways of addressing them

- Explore a wide array of listening strategies employed by active listeners, covering pre-listening strategies, while-listening strategies and post-listening strategies.

Exploring listening resources (1)

- Identify authentic listening materials for long term self- and collaborative learning

- Learn how to deliver information to a target audience

General introduction to stress, rhythm and intonation

- Deepen students’ understanding of the features of spoken English: stress, rhythm and intonation

- Allow students to appreciate the appropriate use of these linguistic features for effective communication in different situations

Critical listening

- Learn how to listen for ideas, viewpoints and personal stance from authentic sources such as news documentary programmes

- Learn how to respond to viewpoints critically through group discussion

Recreational listening

- Learn how to appreciate and respond to language arts by examining the skillful use of language in creating dramatic effects as in sitcoms.

Pair Presentation

- Experience how to organise and lead a group activity

- Provide all members with a wide variety of interesting activities through which they can practice both speaking and listening skills.

Inter-class Debate

- Provide an opportunity for the class to exercise critical listening and response

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: Language Awareness for Teachers 3: Academic Writing
courses.description: This course aims to help students strengthen their academic writing skills through the process approach, as well as appreciate the intimate connection between reading and writing. Specific focuses are placed on critical reading and persuasive writing based on library and Internet research. Coursework will include (1) writing a critical article review and (2) composing a formal argumentative essay. Students will be given opportunities to revise their work after receiving feedback from peers and the instructor.

Learning topics include:

* Genre and audience analysis
* Academic style and tone
* Academic vocabulary
* Advanced sentence structures

2. Preparing for a Research-based Argumentative Essay

* Formulating a research topic
* Conducting library research and documenting sources

APA style consolidation
Avoiding plagiarism

* Forming research-based arguments

Techniques of persuasion
Presenting and justifying arguments
Presenting and rebutting counter-arguments
Writing effective introductory, body and concluding paragraphs

3. Critical Reading & Critical Review Writing

* Introducing critical thinking and critical reading
* Argument analysis and critique (based on educational texts)
* Critical review writing

4. Polishing Your Writing

* Writing concisely and precisely
* Cohesion and coherence
* Effective peer review and editing strategies

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: Language Awareness for Teachers 4: Reading and Writing of Literary Texts
courses.description: This course introduces students to a variety of literary forms in English through the study of selected essays, fiction, drama, and poetry of particular relevance to English language teachers. Students will be required to respond to the readings through reflective journal writing as well as through well developed, coherent essays. The overall aim of the course is to enhance students' power of appreciation of literary works as well as further enhance their writing skills.

3. express appreciation to the different literary forms of work in writing.

courses.subject: ELTU

courses.description: This course aims to develop the English academic writing skills of second-year students from the Contemporary China Studies Program. Students will develop and explore ideas on a topic of their choice before producing a series of descriptive, analytical and persuasive writing that reflects their knowledge of this topic. Coursework will include a range of complementary tasks such as: selecting and incorporating appropriate sources, summarising and critiquing, as well as writing an essay that advances clear and well-supported arguments. Throughout the course students will be engaged in tasks that enhance their academic writing and accuracy of language use. Advisory: For Year 2 students of the Contemporary China Studies Programme only.

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: English through Popular Art and Culture
courses.description:
ELTU3010 English through Popular Art and Culture is a multidisciplinary, interest-oriented level-three course tailored for students from diverse academic backgrounds across the Faculty of Arts at CUHK. The course focuses on developing curation and narration—complementary spoken and written communication skills—to support students’ language development within and beyond their undergraduate studies.

The course emphasises how curation and narration, essential language skills that play a pivotal role in everyday acts of meaning-making, can be applied to popular art and appreciation through a theme-based approach. Themes include, but are not limited to, identity and soul, truth and beauty, pain and trauma, love and hate, explored across disciplines within the settings of Popular Art and Culture. Each theme, delivered as a module, is taught through a variety of popular art forms, such as theatre and drama, television, film and anime, media, documentary, popular music, literature, and the fine arts. Lessons are structured around class activities designed to illustrate the principles of curation and narration using selected sources. Each week, students engage with a diverse range of materials, including readings, video excerpts, songs, and visual or digital art, all aligned with the lesson's theme.

The course also aims to deepen students’ awareness of the humanities—how people understand, interpret, and communicate about the world and their place in it—through engagement with the module themes and class activities. In this course, curation extends beyond traditional gallery, exhibition, or museum contexts to include verbal presentations that involve the selection, organisation, and interpretation of subject matter within Popular Art and Culture. Narration refers to the written articulation, based on the verbal presentation, that structures and conveys meaning through analysis and storytelling. Upon completing the course, students will have acquired the ability to adapt and integrate these spoken and written communication strategies into their own areas of study and interest, enhancing their discipline-specific presentation and expression. They will develop not only linguistic competence but also creative confidence in expressing ideas across cultural and artistic contexts.

Advisory: Year 3 students of the Faculty of Arts.
courses.enrollment_requirement: Prerequisite: (ELTU1001 or ELTU1002 or exemption from these courses) and (ELTU2004 or ELTU2005 or ELTU2006 or ELTU2011 or ELTU2022 or ELTU2406 or ELTU2412 or exemption from these courses)
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

1. Develop the skill of applying fact-led and voice-led verbal presentation and written narration across a range of popular artworks chosen for critical analysis.
2. Verbally articulate and present, with structure and clarity, their selection, organisation, and interpretation of a chosen theme and topic within Popular Art and Culture.
a. Demonstrate critical thinking and analytical skills in their verbal presentation, including the application of relevant disciplinary knowledge.
3. Effectively convey, in written form, a structured and coherent narration of their chosen theme and topic within Popular Art and Culture.
a. Demonstrate storytelling ability and analytical thinking in their written narration.
courses.course_syllabus:
Learning topics include:

Module 1 - Introduction to the Principles of Curation & Narration in Popular Art & Culture: “Identity & Soul Searching”
Module 2 – Narration: “Truth & Beauty”
Module 3 – Subject-specific Expressions and Vocabulary: “Pain & Trauma”
Module 4 – Curation & Curatorial Practice: “Love & Hate”

courses.subject: ELTU
courses.title: Effective Data-Driven Communication in English for Academic and Professional Contexts
courses.description: This course seeks to equip undergraduate students across various disciplines to develop persuasive data-driven spoken and written communication in English for academic and professional purposes. Students will learn how to describe, interpret and apply different data visualization and storytelling techniques to deliver quantitative information across physical and virtual contexts, in both academic and professional communicative settings. Emphasis will be placed on language precision, clarity in visual design, and adaptability of communication strategies to different audiences and communicative goals (e.g., informing, justifying, recommending, advocating).
courses.enrollment_requirement:
Prerequisites:
ELTU1001 or 1002 or exemption from these courses AND
ELTU2004 or 2005 or 2006 or 2011 or 2013 or 2014 or 2016 or 2017 or 2018 or 2019 or 2020 or 2022 or 2023 or 2024 or 2026 or 2406 or 2412 or exemption from these courses
courses.learning_outcomes:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Demonstrate clarity, concision and coherence in data-driven communication that informs and persuades in both academic and professional contexts.
2. Evaluate and select appropriate visualization types that effectively support key messages and persuasive goals for specific data sets in different communicative contexts, both physical and virtual.
3. Critically evaluate visuals for clarity, accuracy, potential bias and persuasive effects.
4. Develop clear data-driven narratives that communicate insights, support claims and justify recommendations.
5. Adapt data-rich content and persuasive strategies for different communicative purposes (e.g., to inform, justify, recommend or advocate) and audiences.
6. Develop rhetorical literacy in the context of AI-human collaborative writing.
courses.course_syllabus:
Learning topics include:

1. Intentional design and persuasive communication of data in academic and professional contexts
2. Audience awareness and purpose: informing, convincing and motivating action with data
3. Writing data commentaries that interpret, evaluate and argue from quantitative evidence
4. Effective data visualization and storytelling for persuasion in reports, posters and presentations
5. Ethical data visualization and avoiding misleading or manipulative use of data
courses.feedback_evaluation:
1. Post-course questionnaire (PCQ)
2. Course and teaching evaluation (CTE) questionnaire
